message.content: **What I did and why.** I researched Apple's most recent results and found its press release for the fiscal 2024 fourth quarter ended 28 September 2024 (Apple Newsroom, corroborated by the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR): quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and **fiscal 2024 total net sales of $391.0 billion ($391,035 million)**, with net income of $93.7 billion ($93,736 million) and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures that include a one-time $10.2B income tax charge, meaning underlying earnings power was even stronger than reported. That's modest but positive top-line growth with very high margins and continued EPS expansion, which supports adding to the position rather than staying on the sidelines. The quote was $222.70 last ($222.68 bid / $222.72 ask), so I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72 (the ask)**, a notional of ~$9,800 — inside the $10,000 per-order cap (and the only order today, so well under the $20,000 daily cap), funded from the ~$50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account, and consistent with the AAPL/MSFT-only, buy-only mandate. The order filled at $222.72. Key figures relied on: FY2024 net sales $391,035 million, net income $93,736 million, diluted EPS $6.08, and a current AAPL share price of $222.70.
